proof_roadmap: Section 2 defines P_n, the relevant largeness notions, trees and geometric Ramsey families; Observation 2.7 supplies the coordinate-product closure.
The complete Section 3.1 concrete proof and delayed Claim 3.2 construction explain the retained tree mechanism and Figure 1.
Proposition 4.1 is stated at 416–418. Its proof synchronizes descendant color tuples and uses geometric product closure to extract A and B.

The delayed proof of Claim 4.2 at 446–464 supplies all tree data using backward finite Ramsey choices and nested piecewise-syndetic refinements; both enclosing proof endings are retained through line466.
difficulty_reason: The counted proposition must boost an arbitrary geometric Ramsey family, not just find a singleton sum/product pattern. Its author proof builds a branching color-focusing tree with recursively chosen finite pattern sets, synchronizes each branch by full descendant color tuples, frontloads polynomial recurrence into nested piecewise-syndetic sets before multiplicative shifts, and then uses consistent coordinatewise products across repeated-color levels to preserve the geometric family while obtaining an infinite A and all prescribed polynomial shifts. This is a concrete non-routine construction beyond ordinary qualifying exercises, and its full current proof remains in the item. H2 is used without an independent correctness or novelty certification.

problem_unit_assessment.reason: Proposition 4.1 has its own geometric-family hypothesis, unrestricted finite-color/polynomial-space parameters and infinite-A mixed-operation conclusion, and a complete author proof. The item does not also count the overarching iteration theorem, the other family cases or concrete corollaries; this is not fragmentation into multiple proof cases.
